chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār, from some of our companions, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Do not betray your leaders, and do not deceive your guides, and do not be ignorant of your Imams عليهم السلام, and do not split away from your bond, lest you fail and your strength depart. Upon this, let the foundation of your affairs be, and adhere to this path.

For if you were to behold what those of you who have died have beheld—those who opposed that to which you are being called—you would hasten, come forth, and listen. But what they have seen is veiled from you, and soon the veil will be cast aside.

key_terms.أَئِمَّتَكُمْ: your Imams, the divinely guided leaders
key_terms.الطَّرِيقَةَ: the path or method that must be adhered to
key_terms.الْحِجَابُ: the veil separating one from unseen realities
key_terms.حَبْلِكُمْ: your bond or rope of unity and connection
key_terms.هُدَاتَكُمْ: your guides who direct you to the truth
key_terms.وُلَاتَكُمْ: your leaders or authorities who hold rightful charge over you

ai.seo_question: What does Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام teach about loyalty to the Imams and the consequences of division?
ai.summary: This hadith is an exhortation to remain loyal to rightful leadership, avoid deceiving divinely guided authorities, and maintain unity around the Imams عليهم السلام. It warns that division brings weakness, and it reminds the listener that after death the realities of obedience and مخالفة become manifest, though they are presently veiled from the living.
